adopted_by: operator decision (option (b) of reports/MAIN_STUDY_PLAN_V5.md 3.4), executed on the server
adopted_after: Claude review round 2 on data/draft-v4.6 (review/v6, reports/ai-review-v6-outcome.json) had been completed and its results seen: 600/600 item judgments consistent, 9 checklist rows issue=yes from single sessions. No pilot, calibration or main run had been started.
not_retroactive: Rounds 1 (review/v5) and 2 (review/v6) were certified/refused under v4-ai-review-1; their outcomes and files are unchanged. This amendment applies from its adoption time onward.
reason: Under v4-ai-review-1 any single issue=yes row forced a data revision and a full six-session re-review. Round 1 -> round 2 reduced 24 flags to 9, all of them single-session, meaning-level or design-level flags rather than grammatical errors; repeating full rounds does not converge because each round yields new single-session flags. The amended rule keeps every flag on record and requires a recorded, independent issue-level adjudication per flag instead of automatic revision.

procedure: every issue=yes row must be covered by exactly one recorded fresh Claude session that judges that issue only (compact package: flagged rows, peer rows, task definition, relevant examples, vocabulary rows)

the session returns a structured verdict: issue_id, reviewed input hashes, scope (primary/auxiliary/documentation), concrete error or counterexample, blocking with rationale, minimal fix or interpretation scope
a blocking verdict fails certification and requires a data revision of the affected part only; unchanged evidence is reused by hash and scope
a non-blocking verdict is carried into the certification report as a recorded limitation; auxiliary-only limits restrict how auxiliary scores may be interpreted
single flags are never dismissed for being single; a peer session's silence never passes a flag; original flags are never edited
item-level rules (200 items per language, agreement >= .95, kappa >= .8, fluent=no and label disagreements adjudicated, labels never changed) are unchanged
